comparator.name: Wiskunde (Mathematics)
comparator.sourceNotes: The ordinary Mathematics pathway closes 60+60+60 with 82.5 EC compulsory study, one selected 7.5-EC modelling course, 15 EC restricted choice, 30 EC further mathematics choice and 45 EC genuine profiling. The selected set meets the 30-EC major level-3 minimum. Modelling preparation is treated as advisory rather than invented as a hard prerequisite. Mathematics and Applications is not substituted. Formal instruction is Dutch plus English.

questionsApplications.label: How can mathematical structures and models explain and predict complex real-world systems?

alternatives.concept: Develop calculus, linear algebra, numerical methods, probability and linear systems through programming, logic, algorithms, optimisation, statistical learning and empirical stochastic models. This is the strongest applied and computational response to the stated Mathematics interests; proof-intensive analysis, algebra, geometry, topology and mathematical research remain explicit gaps.

alternatives.labelRationale: The completed curriculum contains a sustained mathematical and computational spine with concrete algorithmic and stochastic applications, while the label avoids claiming the target programme’s proof-intensive pure-mathematics depth.

alternatives.concept: Use calculus, linear algebra, numerical methods, probability, differential and linear-system models, programming and scientific data analysis to study Earth systems, climate, water–mineral processes, resources and renewable-energy systems. This answers the explicit mathematics-for-climate direction without presenting Earth science as full Mathematics equivalence.

alternatives.labelRationale: Thirteen mathematical/computational courses form the method spine, while ten Earth, climate, resource and energy courses supply coherent scientific systems to model and analyse.
alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Ten courses / 75 EC differ from the closest programme. The Earth-systems route replaces economics, general research methods, optimisation, networks, advanced algorithms, human-data statistics, decision-making and reinforcement learning with sustainability foundations, Earth-system analysis, field/laboratory environmental science, climate, resources and energy technology.

alternatives.concept: Apply calculus, linear algebra, numerical methods, probability, statistics, optimisation and data modelling to economics, corporate finance, strategic interaction, public policy and econometrics. This responds to the explicit mathematics-for-economics and financial-mathematics directions while preserving the absence of a dedicated financial-mathematics or proof-intensive pure-mathematics sequence.

alternatives.labelRationale: The completed curriculum retains a substantial mathematics, statistics, computation and optimisation spine while adding finance, macroeconomics, microeconomics, public economics and econometrics, so the label names mathematics, economics and quantitative decision models together.
alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Against the applied computational route, five courses / 37.5 EC in each direction change: networks, image processing, linear systems, robotics and deep learning are replaced by accounting and corporate finance, ethics, public economics, international macroeconomics and advanced microeconomics. Against the Earth-systems route, fourteen courses / 105 EC differ in each direction. These changes follow from making economic and financial decision models, rather than technological or Earth systems, the application centre.

progressionAssessment.rationale: The schedule contains 24 unique courses, PPD in year one and nine advanced courses. Every formal prerequisite occurs earlier and every course is available in its assigned Fall 2026 cohort semester. Programming precedes algorithms and autonomous decisions; Mathematical Methods precedes dependent mathematics, robotics and neural networks. Research Methods & Statistics precedes Econometrics, while Probability & Statistics and Statistics & Experimental Methods precede the final empirical modelling work.

alternativeSelection.assessment: Three complete related-fields programmes pass the evidence, coherence, course-content, pairwise distinctness and feasibility gates. The closest route integrates mathematical methods with algorithms, optimisation, probability and data models. The second uses the explicit climate direction to organise a materially different Earth-system and scientific-data curriculum.
